items.text: Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year on year, against analyst expectations of about $109.3 billion. Adjusted EPS was $2.68 versus an expected $2.47. It guided Q4 revenue to about $130 billion (plus or minus 3%) against a roughly $125 billion consensus. The outlook assumes no data-center compute revenue from China. Interim CEO Colette Kress, in her first report since Huang's exit, raised the fiscal 2028 growth outlook to about 75% from 70%. The shares closed down 0.4% but rose roughly 2–5% after hours.
items.notes: Reports differ on the size of the after-hours gain: Yahoo/Benzinga says about 2%, Kaohoon about 5%, and Stock Titan 4.8%. The figures come from company results as relayed by outlets. Nvidia's own press release was not read.

items.text: Nvidia board chairman Harvey Jones said on the results day that the board will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and is searching for a permanent replacement. He declined to discuss the investigation into Huang's departure. This cuts against the FT-reported campaign by Silicon Valley allies for Huang's return.
items.notes: Two outlets report it consistently. No direct board statement was read.

items.text: The Pan American Health Organization formally announced on Nov 17 that the US has lost the measles-elimination status it has held since 2000, after one strain circulated for more than 12 months. CDC figures show 5,412 cases in 2026 and 48 outbreaks, and states report 10 deaths. CDC, HHS, PAHO and five public-health groups (ASTHO, APHL, BCHC, CSTE, NACCHO) issued a joint statement pledging to regain the status, citing about $100 million in extra funding to states and a decline in kindergarten MMR coverage to about 92–93%. HHS Secretary Kennedy said on X that the US will work to regain the status and that he still recommends the MMR vaccine.
items.notes: The CDC joint statement includes a quote from PAHO Director Barbosa. The PAHO page itself was not read. A Sight Magazine headline says Mexico and Bolivia also lost their status, but the article could not be fetched (unverified). KVIA, Stateline and CNN pages were blocked.

items.text: The White House withdrew Heidi Overton's nomination as FDA commissioner on Tuesday evening, hours before the Senate HELP Committee was due to vote on Nov 18. ABC cites sources saying several Republican senators objected to her positions on abortion, vaccines and vaping. BioSpace notes her backing for Trump's August order seeking separate single-disease measles, mumps and rubella shots. The FDA has had no permanent commissioner since Marty Makary left in May, and Kyle Diamantas remains acting commissioner. Semafor floated Sen. Roger Marshall as a possible replacement.
items.notes: Axios broke the story and a White House official confirmed it to ABC and The Hill. The Hill page could not be fetched. The Marshall replacement idea is Semafor's, reported via BioSpace.

items.text: NSANet, the NSA's classified internal communications network, suffered an outage on Nov 17, first reported by CNN. The NSA called it temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance and said mission-critical capabilities stayed operational. Secretary of State and NSA adviser Rubio said there was zero evidence that hackers or hostile actors were behind the recent disruptions. DNI Jay Clayton blamed simultaneous upgrades and patching across government and industry. Sen. Mark Warner said the evidence so far points to legitimate security work but the incidents still need investigating. Markets reacted badly to the initial report.
items.notes: The outage is confirmed by the NSA. The cause is the NSA's own claim and has not been independently verified. It comes days after the FAA ground stop, which also had no confirmed cause.

items.text: US stocks fell on Tuesday. CNBC figures relayed by Stock Titan show the Dow down 1.64% (more than 800 points), the Nasdaq down 0.74% and the S&P 500 down about 1%, its lowest close since late July. Traders sold chips ahead of Nvidia's results, and the CNN report of the NSA network outage also weighed. Home Depot fell 2.5% after naming a new CEO and reporting Q3 results.
items.notes: Index point levels were not given. The CNBC live page could not be fetched. The Home Depot CEO name is not confirmed, because the press release found was from 2025.

items.text: Iran's IRGC launched a third drone attack in five days on a US-operated radar at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa air base. CENTCOM said the drones were intercepted with no damage or casualties. Hours later, a US official told Al Jazeera that US strikes hit a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz. A local Iranian official said no civilian areas were damaged. Kuwait reported hostile drone attacks without naming a source. AP says Washington is weighing a return to all-out strikes or a tighter blockade, while Qatari mediation remains stalled.
items.notes: The Qeshm strike rests on an unnamed US official speaking to Al Jazeera and on Iranian local officials. The AP version (Boston Globe) did not report any US retaliation. CENTCOM confirmed the intercept.

items.text: Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday evening after more than 18 hours of travel, for the ASEAN–US special summit and talks with President Marcos at Malacañang on Wednesday. At the summit he said US–Philippine ties are closer than ever because of his personal relationship with Marcos, told ASEAN leaders to call him when there is a problem, and pointed to proposals for more joint special-forces training. He again suggested a meeting with Kim Jong Un could happen. Next he goes to APEC in Shenzhen, where the Kremlin and Beijing say a first-ever Trump–Xi–Putin trilateral meeting is set for Nov 19.
items.notes: The outcome of the Marcos bilateral meeting was not yet reported in the sources read. The trilateral date was confirmed by Peskov on Nov 14 (Anadolu: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/eurasia/kremlin-says-putin-xi-trump-to-hold-trilateral-meeting-in-shenzhen-on-nov-19/4125290). The Quad leaders' meeting in Manila is left to the US–India desk. NBC, CNN and Philstar pages were blocked or errored.

items.text: On the sidelines of the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila, Trump and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul signed a joint trade statement. Trump said a formal agreement would be finalised in the coming weeks and that Thailand would eliminate tariffs on US exports and buy $2.6 billion of US farm products.
items.notes: The terms come from Trump's account in the ABC live blog. No Thai government or USTR text was found.

items.text: Bloomberg reports that Anthropic is guiding its IPO to price at or above the top of its $70–78 range, with orders near seven times the shares on offer. The WSJ says pricing could exceed $80. At $78 the deal would raise about $90.4 billion, counting a $26 billion private placement, at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion. Books closed at 4 p.m. ET on Nov 17. Pricing is expected Nov 18 and Nasdaq trading (ANT) Nov 19.
items.notes: Based on unnamed sources. Bloomberg is paywalled and was not read directly. CNBC reports the same (page not fetchable).

items.text: US District Judge Julia Kobick in Boston blocked two August DHS directives that had narrowed curricular practical training (CPT) for foreign students to training required of every student in a programme. She found them likely arbitrary and capricious because DHS did not acknowledge it was changing a long-standing interpretation. The suit was brought by groups including the Association of American Universities. About 140,000 student-visa holders were authorised for CPT in 2024. DHS declined to comment.
items.notes: Law360 (link2) is paywalled and was not read.

items.text: Peltola now has 141,637 first-choice votes (49.98%) to Sen. Dan Sullivan's 130,162 (45.93%), about 52 votes short of an outright majority, with AP estimating 98% counted. Sullivan's campaign broke its silence on Facebook, saying it would let the count run to certification and would have more to say by the end of the week. Overseas ballots are due Nov 18, when the final count and any ranked-choice tabulation are scheduled. Certification is targeted for Nov 25.
items.notes: Unofficial Division of Elections figures relayed by Newsweek. The tabulation itself had not happened by the time of this sweep (it falls on Alaska's Nov 18).

items.text: Ahead of the Dec 11 funding deadline, Sens. Bennet, Sanders, Van Hollen and Duckworth say they will oppose any stopgap that lets Iran-war funding continue, and Sen. Tim Kaine is drafting language to block it. On the House side, several Republicans say they will block Trump's $350 billion defense reconciliation package unless the White House takes a tougher line on Russia. House and Senate Armed Services leaders meet twice this week on a compromise NDAA, after a $1.15 trillion request.
items.notes: HNGN is a secondary aggregator. These points were not cross-checked with Roll Call, AP or Politico.

items.text: NASA said Terra, the flagship Earth Observing System satellite launched in December 1999 for a six-year mission, will stop collecting science data on Dec 1 after 27 years because its systems are ageing and its orbit is drifting. The team will use its remaining fuel to lower the orbit and power it off in January 2027. Its archive (MODIS, ASTER, MISR, CERES, MOPITT) stays freely available.
items.notes: NASA's post names no successor missions and gives no budget context.

items.text: The General Assembly of Constitutional Tribunal (TK) judges called by Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska met on Nov 17 to consider Prosecutor General Waldemar Żurek's motions to lift the immunity of TK President Bogdan Święczkowski and Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański, including consent to detain and arrest Święczkowski (alleged offences relate to Pegasus, the Hermes purchase, obstructing TK judges and unlawful delegations of prosecutors). Święczkowski came to the TK building at 9:00, was not let in, called the meeting a 'social gathering' and refused to attend the noon hearing, which was held at the Warsaw District Court; his and Sochański's lawyers attended and raised procedural objections, then the assembly returned to the TK. The TK website said the outcome will be announced on Nov 18. Six judges including Święczkowski and Sochański issued a statement saying the assembly was convened by an unauthorised person, lacked a quorum and its decisions have no legal effect. Polsat News reports the ECHR unanimously refused the two judges an interim measure against their suspension.
items.notes: Outcome not yet published as of morning Nov 18; a KO MP (Matusik-Lipiec) posted that immunity was lifted, unconfirmed. Number of judges attending not reported. Framing: Nasz Dziennik (right) calls participants 'usurpers' and stresses unaddressed defence motions (https://naszdziennik.pl/polska-kraj/348816,nie-rozpoznano-wnioskow-obroncow-prezesa-i-wiceprezesa-trybunalu.html); TVN24 live coverage relied mostly on Święczkowski's own statements; Rzeczpospolita/PAP neutral. Wprost, Bankier and goniec.pl pages could not be read. ECHR refusal reported by Polsat (citing Żurek and MFA spokesman), not checked against ECHR site.

items.text: The Sejm rejected a constructive vote of no confidence in Donald Tusk's government filed by Mateusz Morawiecki's Rozwój Plus club, which proposed Marek Jurek as prime minister. The vote was 200 for, 242 against, with 18 not voting; 231 votes were needed. Morawiecki cited the government's actions on the Constitutional Tribunal and rising unemployment; Tusk mocked the choice of Jurek. Konfederacja voted for while saying it expected failure; Polska 2050, the Left and Razem opposed, and about ten PiS deputies did not vote.
items.notes: Tally confirmed by official Sejm voting record (sitting 69, vote 7, print 3354).

items.text: Presidential spokesman Rafał Leśkiewicz said President Nawrocki will carry out the government changes on Friday Nov 20 at 11:00: Andrzej Domański as deputy prime minister and Agnieszka Bartol as minister of funds and regional policy, replacing Katarzyna Pełczyńska-Nałęcz. Earlier the same day the head of the President's Chancellery, Zbigniew Bogucki, said the changes would have happened long ago but for what he called the government's attack on the Tribunal on the night of Oct 30–31, and that there was no deadline for the President. Government spokesman Adam Szłapka said the President has no discretion and is breaking the constitution by delaying.
items.notes: PAP text says '20 grudnia' once (typo; headline and Friday reference give Nov 20). No mention of the four NBP board appointments. Leśkiewicz said scope depended on the no-confidence vote outcome.

items.text: Speaking in the Sejm a day after the first Belweder round, PM Tusk said the currently sitting Constitutional Tribunal judges were lawfully elected and that the renewed Tribunal has started work, though with difficulty. He said he was open to any initiative and did not hold PSL leader Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz or Szymon Hołownia's search for solutions against them, but agreed PSL's 'reset' proposal, which KO, the Left and PiS do not back, may not be realistic. The second Belweder meeting chaired by Bogucki is set for Nov 18 at 17:00; no report was found of the combined Chancellery draft promised for Nov 17.
items.notes: Only Rzeczpospolita read; whether the Chancellery's combined draft was actually circulated on Nov 17 could not be confirmed.

items.text: The Council of Ministers adopted the Energy Ministry's bill (UD501) freezing the gas price at 197.29 zł/MWh net (excluding VAT, excise and distribution) for all of 2027 for about 7.5 million households, housing cooperatives and communities, and public-interest institutions such as schools, hospitals, care homes, churches and shelters. Sellers are compensated via a fund financed by a 10% levy on net revenues of large gas importers (firms with under 10% of entry capacity exempt); compensation is put at about 4.6bn zł in 2027 and 1.6bn zł in 2028, about 6.2bn zł in total. URE tariffs stay for protected customers until end-2030. Tusk said the fuel price programme (CPN) will continue and work on electricity prices goes on; Energy Minister Motyka hopes the bill reaches the President in early December, and the Sejm first reading is planned for Nov 19.
items.notes: ISBnews cites the Energy Ministry statement; savings 77–1,863 zł/yr per household. First-reading date from Infor.pl preliminary Sejm schedule.

items.text: The government adopted a bill amending the law on trust services and electronic identification to implement eIDAS 2.0 and introduce the European Digital Identity Wallet, initially offered inside the mObywatel app. It would let people prove facts such as identity, age or driving entitlement without sharing documents, including proof of being over 18 without revealing a birth date. Use is voluntary for citizens, but banks, telecoms, transport, healthcare firms and very large online platforms must accept it where strong authentication is required; the Digital Affairs Minister supervises and could suspend a qualified trust service for up to 14 days.
items.notes: EU deadline to offer a wallet is roughly December 2026; no parliamentary timetable given.

items.text: President Nawrocki signed the act on personal assistance for people with disabilities. Adults aged 18–65 can apply from 2028 and young people from age 13 from 2030, for up to 240 hours of assistance a month depending on need, granted for one to five years. The person chooses the tasks and can pick their assistant; the service is run by county governments or NGOs, and about 100,000 people are expected to use it.
items.notes: Cost and entry-into-force date not given in RMF24; prezydent.pl not checked directly.

items.text: The Sejm rejected, 197 to 227 with 5 abstentions, motions by PiS, Razem, Demokracja Bezpośrednia and two independents to throw out at first reading the Senate's bill abolishing the two-term limit for mayors, wójts and city presidents. The bill, which would also repeal the 2018 transitional rule, goes to the extraordinary committee on codification changes. A separate PSL bill on the same issue failed 213–215 on Oct 22.

The Sejm held the second reading of the government's reimbursement law amendment (about 175 changes): a national Critical Medicines List, a larger patient discount (30% instead of 15%) for drugs made in Poland, multi-criteria assessment of orphan drugs, an AOTMiT catalogue of equivalent therapies and spending caps for drugs without equivalents; OTC drugs would be dropped from reimbursement. KO, Centrum and Razem filed amendments, including easing producers' penalties for shortages (KO), exempting vaccines from automatic price cuts (Centrum) and making fully Polish-made reimbursed drugs free (Razem). The bill went back to the Health Committee.
items.notes: PiS, Konfederacja and Razem broadly support the direction; Rozwój Plus warns innovative drugs may be available only on paper. Free-drugs idea is only a Razem amendment.

items.text: Poland drew 1–1 with Sweden in Wrocław in its final UEFA Nations League League B group match, after losing 1–2 in Romania on Saturday ended its hopes of a promotion play-off to League A.
items.notes: Scorers not listed on the stats page.

items.text: City Hall presented a draft resolution that would shrink Kraków's Clean Transport Zone (SCT) from about 196 km² to about 0.99 km², roughly the area inside the first ring road (Planty/Basztowa) plus a strip along Piłsudskiego, al. Krasińskiego and Zwierzyniecka so that the Krasińskiego air-monitoring station stays inside. Emission standards would not change. The residents' exemption would no longer require registration in Kraków, only paying income tax there. It would also cover company, leased and rented cars and visits to any medical facility in the zone. Paid windscreen stickers (5 zł) would be replaced by number-plate checks. Deputy Mayor Jan Hoffman said the change could take effect in February or March 2027, after at least 21 days of public consultation and two readings in the council. He expects the KO majority to back it. Current rules and boundaries apply until then.
items.notes: Also reported by KRKnews, Kurier Krakowski and Interia. The city cites a 9 Jul 2025 GIOŚ letter: the NO₂ exceedance near al. Krasińskiego covered about 0.2 km² and 9,387 residents under the old 40 µg/m³ limit. SmogLab (6 Nov), citing GIOŚ 2025 data, says about 684,000 residents live where NO₂ exceeds the new, stricter EU standard. The two figures use different limits. The official krakow.pl notice ('Strefa Czystego Transportu: miasto proponuje zmiany', 17 Nov) could not be fetched. No consultation start date has been given.

items.text: Clean-air groups criticised the plan to shrink the SCT. Krakowski Alarm Smogowy warned that a zone limited to the centre would lose much of its effect, because traffic emissions also affect busy arteries outside it. Akcja dla Krakowa had earlier accused the new authorities of retreating from health protections. Głos24 notes that the city's timeline no longer mentions the referendum on the zone's future that Gibała promised and that the 23 Sep Gibała–Hoffman pact committed to. Hoffman told TVN24 that residents should decide the final shape of the zone in a referendum or other vote within a year or two.
items.notes: Dziennik Polski has a story headlined with SCT supporters calling it a joke at the expense of their health, but the page would not load. KRKnews reports that comments under Gibała's post were split. Lawyers quoted by Głos24 question whether a referendum can override an obligation set by statute.

items.text: Deputy Mayor Karol Wałachowski said the city is pausing preparations for a metro because no construction funding has been secured. It will concentrate on trams instead, but would build the metro if national or EU money appears. He ordered an analysis of how much has already been spent. The geological-survey tender is stuck at an appeal before the National Appeals Chamber (KIO). Councillor Michał Starobrat said about 200m zł for design will stay in the multi-year financial forecast.
items.notes: Głos24's story on the 2027 budget also says the metro is being dropped as too costly. The spending total is not yet known.

items.text: More night closures are planned on the A4 Kraków bypass. At the Modlniczka junction, slip roads towards Zabierzów close from 20:00 to 06:00 on 17/18 Nov, with more nights on 18/19, 19/20, 20/21, 23/24 and 24/25 Nov. At the Kraków Skawina junction, rolling night closures of individual slip roads start on 19/20 Nov and run until 2/3 Dec, with detours via the Tyniec or Łagiewniki junctions. A 110 km/h limit applies on the A4 near Skawina around the clock. The GDDKiA schedule puts completion of the Skawina work at 11 Dec. These closures add to the single-lane restriction near the Skawina–Południe viaduct from 18 to 20 Nov.
items.notes: Based on the GDDKiA schedule as reported by KRKnews; not checked against GDDKiA's own site.

items.text: Przemysław Nowak, spokesman for the National Prosecutor's Office, told PAP that the closest relative of the 7 Nov attacker, 24-year-old Michał Oksiński, has asked to collect the body for a funeral. The body will be released after further examinations are finished. This makes Mayor Gibała's plan to offer the body to UJ Collegium Medicum, and the city's possible duty to pay for a burial, unlikely to be needed.
items.notes: KRKnews cites PAP. The relative's identity is not given. No news on motive or CCTV.

items.text: Gdańsk police said a 27-year-old local man was detained on 12 Nov after posting on social media that he had been in contact with the Kraków attacker and knew where similar attacks could happen. He was charged with reporting a false alarm, which carries up to 8 years in prison. The Gdańsk-Śródmieście prosecutor put him under police supervision and banned him from posting content that could make people fear a crime.
items.notes: Based on a Gdańsk regional police statement. The detention took place on 12 Nov and was reported on 17 Nov.

items.text: Early reactions to the 2027 draft budget: Michał Starobrat, councillor for Gibała's 'Kraków dla Mieszkańców' club, welcomed the decision to design a tram to Kliny and says the previous administration's plan implied a deficit of about 1.5bn zł. Krakowski Raport questions the claimed 300m zł in savings, because the first city statement gave specific amounts for only about 75m zł. Kurier Krakowski and KR24 note that debt still rises by about 927m zł, capital spending falls by about 170m zł to 1.535bn zł, and culture and sport lines shrink. Council support is not assured. The KO/Lewica majority had not given a formal response by the time of these reports.
items.thread: Kraków city finances and the 2027 budget
items.notes: No statements from KO, PiS or Lewica found. Starobrat's 1.5bn zł figure cannot be checked. Głos24 (17 Nov) also lists the projects coming back: tram designs for Kliny, Lema, Azory–Bronowice Wielkie and others, and refurbishing more than 500 empty municipal flats.

items.text: The 64th session of Kraków City Council opens at 11:00 today and is streamed on RMK Live. It begins by honouring medics who helped after the 7 Nov attack. Second readings include the fare resolution (druk 1587), which would bring back a 4 zł 20-minute ticket and other time tickets from 4 Jan 2027 and add an annual ticket for doctoral students, at an estimated cost of about 19.6m zł a year in lost revenue. Also up for second reading: suspending the Lviv partnership (druk 1586), towing fees and the Piaski Nowe local plan. First readings cover the 2027 property tax rates (1.49 zł/m² for business land, 1.29 zł/m² for residential buildings) and vehicle tax rates. The agenda also includes information from the mayor on the SCT fee freeze, the withdrawal resolutions for Eurocities and other associations (druki 1628-1636), 2026 budget amendments (druki 1622-1626), the vote on starting consultations on ending discounted sales of municipal flats (druk 1618), and the residents' draft on nursery grants. No results had been published at the time of research.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Preview only, based on the BIP agenda. Results should be checked this afternoon or evening. LoveKraków, Radio Kraków and krakow.pl pages could not be opened (fetch permission timed out).

items.text: The council's Main Committee unanimously backed Mayor Gibała's motion to make senior constables Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, both wounded responding to the 7 Nov attack, honorary citizens of Kraków. The item is not yet on the session agenda because of two rules: a limit of five honorary citizenships per term (three already awarded) and a 31 March application deadline that has passed. The two officers, still in hospital, also have to give consent. Council officials expect to fix the procedural problems within about a week and then add the item.
items.notes: The publication date is not shown. The 16 Nov date is inferred from the committee meeting on Monday.

items.text: The 11th Open Eyes Economy Summit runs on 17–18 Nov at ICE Kraków under the theme 'Business and democracy', opened by Mayor Gibała. Announced guests include Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, ESA astronaut Sławosz Uznański-Wiśniewski, Marek Belka, BGK president Mirosław Czekaj and Thuringia's Minister-President Mario Voigt. The fifth edition of the Polish Economic Credibility Index, led by Prof. Jerzy Hausner, is to be presented there.
items.notes: Organiser's press release on PAP MediaRoom. No reporting on what was said at the summit or on the index results was found.

items.text: Prosecutors say an expert reading of the car's data recorder shows the Volkswagen in the August crash on ul. Solna was travelling at about 85 km/h, far above the 30 km/h limit and faster than first established. Blood tests found no alcohol in the driver. Prosecutors released autopsy findings and asked the court to extend his pre-trial detention.
items.notes: Only the RSS summary was read, not the full article.

items.text: The 13th Kraków commemoration of the post-war anti-communist underground ('Żołnierze Wyklęci') took place without its traditional march, which was cancelled after the 7 Nov attack. It included a service at Corpus Christi basilica, testimonies at the Home Army Museum and an honour for 101-year-old poet Jan Lohmann.
items.notes: Only the RSS summary was read.

items.text: A Supreme Court bench led by CJI Surya Kant heard the batch of pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the ECI's SIR decisions on Nov 17 and adjourned them to Dec 9. Kapil Sibal, for Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, said the ECI's Oct 26 affidavit asserts a 'unanimous' decision on the nationwide SIR but attaches no minutes, file notings or approval dates, and asked the court to issue notice on 48 interrogatories to the CEC, ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi and senior officials. Harish Salve, for the ECI, said the commission has serious reservations and opposed any notice before a preliminary hearing. The CJI said the court would first hear the application and then pass orders, and the ECI may file objections by Dec 9.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: LiveLaw's daily round-up headlines say the court 'sought the ECI's response', while The Wire and Revoi say it declined to issue formal notice before hearing the application. The latter wording is used here. No Swarajya or other right-leaning write-up of the hearing was found. A Press News Agency link reporting the Dec 9 date could not be fetched.

items.text: The UP Chief Electoral Officer published the draft electoral roll under the Special Summary Revision 2027 on Nov 17. It lists 13,58,68,905 voters: 7.39 crore men, 6.20 crore women and 4,042 third-gender voters. That is a net increase of 18,84,113 over the post-SIR final roll of Apr 10, including 10.97 lakh more women. The gender ratio rose from 834 to 840 women per 1,000 men, but voters aged 18-19 fell by 5.8 lakh to 11.83 lakh. Claims and objections are open until Dec 16, to be disposed of by Dec 28, and the final roll is due Jan 4, 2027.
items.notes: PTI gives no separate count of deletions, only the net change. DD News (state broadcaster) carries the same figures.

items.text: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav responded to the UP draft roll by accusing the BJP and its allies of using the 'ASDD' (absent, shifted, dead, duplicate) process and Form 6 additions to insert fake voters. He told party booth workers and citizens to check every new name added in their areas. He said any official who adds a name dishonestly should face an FIR, dismissal and loss of pension. In comments reported by Republic Bharat, he said a rise in voters is welcome but warned against what he called conspiracy. No BJP response was reported in the articles read.
items.notes: These are claims by a party leader, not evidence of irregularities. Republic Bharat (right-leaning) was seen only as a search headline.

items.text: Cyclone Akvan intensified into a severe cyclonic storm on the evening of Nov 17, according to Odisha's relief commissioner citing IMD. IMD's 02:30 IST Nov 18 bulletin placed it about 620 km SSE of Visakhapatnam, moving slowly north. IMD forecasts a very severe cyclonic storm by Nov 19 and a crossing of the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on Nov 20, with winds of 120–130 km/h gusting to 145 km/h. It warns of a 0.4–1.2 m storm surge in Prakasam, Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, Konaseema, Kakinada and Visakhapatnam districts, and of extremely heavy rain in coastal AP on Nov 19–20. CM Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan reviewed preparations on Nov 17 and ordered evacuation of low-lying coastal areas, relief camps and protection of tanks and canals. This is the third cyclone to hit the state in weeks, after Arnab and Murasu.
items.notes: IMD's landfall window now reads Nellore–Visakhapatnam (earlier Nellore–Tuni). IMD rates its track and intensity confidence as moderate, and some models, including ECMWF, weaken the storm before landfall. Jagran reports an IMD red alert for seven AP districts. AP evacuation numbers were not yet published.

items.text: Odisha identified 2,04,070 people for possible evacuation ahead of Cyclone Akvan, including 1.22 lakh in Ganjam, 25,000 in Gajapati and 24,076 in Puri. It deployed 74 rescue teams (60 ODRAF and 14 NDRF), with Ganjam getting 15. The state released ₹6.5 crore from the SDRF and has 3,329 cyclone shelters on standby. Fishing is barred from Nov 18 to Nov 20, and IMD orange alerts for heavy rain run across southern districts from Nov 19 to 22. Malkangiri has closed schools, colleges and anganwadis on Nov 19–20, and six districts were told to prepare for landslides.

PM Modi attended the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit in Manila on Nov 17, hosted by Philippine President Marcos Jr. He proposed nine initiatives: free e-visas for ASEAN tourists, a long-term maritime cooperation plan, joint cyber-forensics training, nuclear energy technical exchanges, a space hackathon, a critical-minerals mechanism, a youth programme, more Nalanda University scholarships for ASEAN students, and a creative-industries pavilion at WAVES 2027. Leaders adopted an ASEAN-India Joint Statement on Disaster Management. At the EAS, India offered to host a cybercrime conference at NFSU, a maritime heritage festival at Lothal and a university conclave at Nalanda. Modi also met Marcos, and a Quad leaders' meeting was held on the sidelines.
items.notes: The Quad leaders' meeting in Manila belongs to the US–India agent and is not detailed here. The Modi–Marcos meeting (defence and trade) comes from the TNI headline list only. No date was given for when the free e-visas start.

items.text: The Sensex rose 427.40 points (0.52%) to 82,532.19 and the Nifty 96.30 points (0.38%) to 25,387.40 on Nov 17, a second straight gain, led by realty and PSU banks (up about 2% each). The Bank Nifty hit a record high, while IT fell 0.9%. Breadth was slightly negative and small-caps slipped. HDFC Sky reports foreign investors have now put a record $9.53 billion into Indian equities in November, as funds rotate out of US AI stocks after a 2.5% Nasdaq fall. Brent eased to about $91.70 on expectations of a supply surplus, which helped paint and tyre stocks.
items.notes: The index levels match the TNI and Business Standard headlines. The rupee close was not found for Nov 17.

items.text: Nominations closed on Nov 17 for the Dec 4 elections to Ladakh's eight Autonomous Hill Development Councils: 541 candidates filed for 100 seats, including 276 independents, 126 Congress, 125 BJP and 14 National Conference. The Leh Apex Body is continuing a protest at NDS Park in Leh to demand postponement over winter conditions, and some groups have called a boycott. Sonam Wangchuk says he has been under house detention in Leh since Nov 11 and that his team has petitioned the Leh bench of the J&K and Ladakh High Court against it. The administration has imposed 60-day restrictions on him that bar unauthorised rallies.
items.thread: Ladakh statehood protests and council polls
items.notes: ETV Bharat calls the panchayat and urban polls 'scheduled for Nov 11', which conflicts with other reporting (Daily Pioneer, The Wire) that they are on Nov 21. It is probably an error. No hearing date has been reported for Wangchuk's plea.

items.text: Union Minister of State for Petroleum Suresh Gopi called those alleging excess ethanol in petrol 'idiots' who do not understand science. He said E20 was adopted after ARAI-approved research and that blending equipment cuts off at 20%. He also said that only a CBI probe could establish whether adulteration occurred, and claimed there have been no insurance claims for ethanol-related vehicle damage. His remarks target Karnataka, which reports samples with up to 31.2% ethanol, and Kerala (Keralam), which has begun its own testing with results still awaited. Neither the ministry nor the oil companies have agreed to joint retesting.
items.notes: No Karnataka government reply to Gopi was found yet.

items.text: President Droupadi Murmu opened the year-long golden jubilee of the ICMR-National Institute of Malaria Research in New Delhi on Nov 17, with Health Minister J.P. Nadda present. She noted that India left the WHO 'High Burden to High Impact' malaria group in 2024, crediting diagnostics, drugs, vector control and community participation. She warned that climate change, unplanned urbanisation and rising insecticide resistance in mosquitoes could set back elimination, and that dengue is a growing threat as warming shifts monsoon patterns.
items.notes: No new case numbers or targets were announced.

items.text: MS Dhoni, 45, has retired from playing in the IPL and will be Chennai Super Kings' team mentor from the 2027 season, CSK managing director KS Viswanathan confirmed. Dhoni played 278 IPL matches, scoring 5,439 runs at an average of 38.30, and led CSK to five titles. He missed the whole 2026 season with a calf strain. Separately, double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker was elected to the ISSF Athletes Committee for 2026–30.
items.notes: The Manu Bhaker item comes from the TNI headline list only. TNI also reports that Mohammed Shami moves to Rajasthan Royals for IPL 2027; this was not verified and is not included.

items.text: According to LiveLaw's Supreme Court round-up, the court upheld the stay on SP leader Azam Khan's conviction in the forged birth certificate case and extended the same relief to his wife and son. The same round-up reports that Bilkis Bano said she was shocked by the court's order suspending the sentences of two convicts in her case and that she had not been heard. The Supreme Court Bar Association also sought criminal contempt proceedings against a lawyer over insulting remarks about CJI Surya Kant.
items.notes: Only the paywalled headlines could be read. The TNI headline list separately says the Allahabad HC granted Azam Khan interim bail in a money-laundering case on Nov 17; this was not verified and is not included.

items.text: Trump, Modi, Japan's PM Takaichi and Australia's PM Albanese held the first in-person Quad leaders' summit in two years in Manila on the evening of Nov 17, on the margins of the ASEAN summit. Their joint press release, issued by the White House, opposes destabilising or unilateral attempts to change the status quo by force or coercion. It voices concern about economic coercion, including arbitrary export restrictions, and condemns terrorism, including cross-border terrorism. China is not named. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri called the meeting substantive and pragmatic, and said Modi stressed 'peace, stability and predictability' at all three Manila summits. The release does not name a host or date for the next leaders' summit.
items.notes: The White House release was read in full. The Japan Times page failed to load. No MEA joint-statement page was checked separately.

items.text: No Modi–Trump bilateral or reported pull-aside took place in Manila. Neither the Misri briefing nor the wire reports describe any one-on-one exchange, and trade was not mentioned in the Indian readouts. At the photo-op before the meeting, Trump called Modi 'a very tough man', a great leader and a friend. Trump kept taking reporters' questions while Modi asked the leaders 'Shall we move?', and the video went viral in India. News18 commentators said the delay cut into the roughly 40 minutes set aside for talks.
items.notes: Bloomberg ran a story on the 'awkward' briefing (robots-blocked, not read): https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-18/modi-tries-to-end-photo-op-with-trump-in-awkward-quad-briefing. Inshorts sourced the clip from a post on X. The absence of a bilateral rests on missing reports rather than an official statement, but it matches ThePrint's earlier reporting.

items.text: The Quad leaders launched an Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration to improve information sharing and maritime domain awareness. In 2027, P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft will hold the first maritime exercise in a Quad format. Misri said it will take place in March 2027 in Guam, alongside Exercise Sea Dragon, and will target illegal fishing and trafficking. Trump announced the patrol-aircraft exercise himself at the meeting.
items.notes: The March/Guam detail comes from Misri via IANS; the White House release says only '2027'.

items.text: The Quad endorsed a 'Super Intelligence Accelerator', first announced by Quad foreign ministers in Atlanta, to coordinate and fund access to trusted AI across the Indo-Pacific. A footnote to the release says 'Super Intelligence' means AI in Australia, India and Japan. Trump said the four countries will spend more than $85 million on it. The leaders also agreed to step up cyber-security cooperation in response to rising cyber incidents. Separately, Trump claimed the US would have all the rare earths it needs within 10 months; experts quoted by the Daily Beast called this highly unlikely.
items.notes: The $85m figure appears in Trump's remarks as carried by wire copy, not in the release, so treat it as Single-source/Claimed. The rare-earth timeline is a Claim by Trump (Outlook India, Daily Beast).

items.text: The Quad will hold its first Business Leaders' Forum in early 2027, bringing together business leaders, officials and policy experts to promote commercial deals. Modi announced that Mumbai will host it in the first quarter of 2027. Leaders also expanded the Quad cable partnership to cover undersea electricity cables, with Australia increasing its contribution.
items.notes: The White House release does not name Mumbai; that comes from Modi's announcement in the wire copy.

items.text: The US Labor Department's proposed overhaul of the PERM green-card labour certification was published in the Federal Register on Nov 17, opening a 60-day comment period. It would lengthen minimum recruitment from 30 to 90 days, move advertising online, and bar employers that laid off US workers in a similar role within two years. It would also end the Schedule A shortcut for nurses and physical therapists. Indians make up about 79% of the roughly 1.26 million people in the EB-1/2/3 queues, nearly one million people, so Indian tech workers and nurses are among the most exposed. Current rules stay in force until a final rule is issued.
items.notes: The Federal Register entry itself was not located or read, so the publication date and comment period come from The Week. This may overlap with the US-area log, which owns the rule itself.

items.text: After meeting Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby in Brussels on Nov 17, Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said Colby had confirmed that things are moving in the right direction. He called this a Pentagon 'green light' for a permanent US base in Poland and said he expects the White House to confirm it. He said Colby told him the US review of force posture in Europe is nearly complete and its conclusions go to the White House in early December. Deputy Minister Paweł Zalewski said formal negotiations had been closed during last week's Washington visit, with details to follow the review. There was no US readout, and no location or troop numbers were given.
items.notes: All accounts rely on Polish officials, and rp.pl flags that its headline rests on them. The right-leaning outlets nczas.info and kresy.pl carried the same PAP line with no dissent found. Context: on Nov 16 (before this window), Deputy Minister Sobkowiak-Czarnecka urged President Nawrocki on Radio Zet to lobby Trump, putting the odds at 95% if the decision rested on the Pentagon alone (money.pl).

items.text: At the EU defence ministers' council in Brussels, Kosiniak-Kamysz pushed to open the EU defence market and EU funding to non-EU NATO allies, so that Polish–US joint ventures making American equipment in Poland could qualify. He said Poland and the US are speeding up defence-industrial cooperation under the letter of intent he signed with Hegseth, aiming for more US weapons to be produced and repaired in Poland, including at the planned PAC-3 Patriot service centre. On the margins, Lithuania's defence minister showed interest in the Barracuda-500 missile, which PGZ plans to build in Poland with US firm Anduril.
items.notes: No new detail on the location of the PAC-3 service centre (W-261108-12 remains open). The outcome of the EU council on non-EU allies' access was not reported. milmag.pl was only partly readable.
